$schema_note: docs/roadmap.md's Tier 1-F design: a committed JSON index of every duels-value weights generation, promoted or not, so a retrain is first-class data instead of a hand-pinned hash. Do not edit an entry's measured fields by hand after the fact -- append a new generation or update `status`/`notes`, the same discipline golden.rs's own docs ask for. Archived detail (raw battery records, training logs, corpus manifests) lives at /Volumes/storage/duels/, referenced here by path/label rather than duplicated -- this file is an index, not a database, matching this project's existing convention for corpus .manifest.json sidecars and arena/leaderboard.json.

generations.notes: Tier 1-D/E control: plain argmax generator (no exploration, no specialists), lambda=1.0 (today's exact training target before this experiment). Isolates D and E's effects by being neither. Not promoted -- kept reachable as an ablation baseline via mcts-value:weights=arm-a.

Tier 1-D+E: corpus generated WITH exploration (visits^(1/tau), tau=1, 14 plies) and 25% specialist-seat mixing, lambda=1.0. +32.0 Elo vs v2 at 2,000 games (elo1=10), reproduced at +26.8 Elo on a disjoint seed range (arm-b-vs-v2-nodes2000-confirm). Both accepted, mechanism gate Pass. Was the strongest generation measured until the Tier 1-D/E gradient-bug fix and its retest: tier1-arm-c-prime beats this generation directly by +27.0 Elo (2,000 games, CI excludes zero) and beats v2 by nearly 2x this generation's own margin. Kept reachable via mcts-value:weights=arm-b as the ablation baseline that isolates D's effect from E's.

Tier 1-E: the SAME corpus as arm-b, retrained at value-target-lambda=0.5. Read as -17.2 Elo vs v2 and rejected -- but a later review found tools/train_value.py's two-term-loss gradient for the LOSS logit was wrong ((s-t)/(1-s) instead of s-t; only fires when lambda<1.0), confirmed by finite-difference (tools/test_train_value_grad.py) and by this generation's own training log (divide-by-zero/overflow/invalid-value RuntimeWarnings during the forward/backward pass, and val-loss that never improved past epoch 0 -- unlike arm-a/b, which are unaffected since lambda=1.0 short-circuits the buggy path). This result is therefore NOT a trustworthy reading on the value-target-blend idea and should not be cited as one; see tier1-arm-c-prime for the corrected retest from the same corpus.

generations.notes: Generation 3: the roadmap's 'run it again from v3, see whether the gain per generation holds or decays' follow-up. A fresh ~100k-game corpus (tier1-gen3-explore, disjoint seed range 2,400,001-2,500,000) self-played by the then-champion v3 with the identical exploration+specialist-mixing generator config that produced tier1-arm-bc-explore (--sample-plies 14 --tau 1.0 --specialist-frac 0.25), replay-verified cleanly (every game reproduced) and sealed to /Volumes/storage/duels/ with a checksum comparison against the working copy before training. Trained window=1 (this corpus alone, not combined with tier1-arm-bc-explore -- the roadmap's simpler default, no strong reason found to do otherwise) at this project's production hyperparameters (--hidden 128 --epochs 60 --lr 2e-3 --weight-decay 1e-5 --patience 8), --value-target-lambda 0.5. Trained cleanly, best epoch 20 of 60, val win-logloss 0.50694 (test 0.50313) -- no NaN/divergence. HONEST HEADLINE: this generation's gain over v3 is real but much smaller than v2->v3's (+61.0/+53.9 Elo): the properly pooled gating cell across two disjoint seed ranges (4,000 games total, elo1=10) reads +17.2 Elo [+6.4, +28.0], AcceptH1, mechanism Pass -- but the two individual ranges disagreed sharply before pooling (+29.6 AcceptH1 on the first, +4.9 Continue/Inconclusive on the second), and the TimeMs(1000) cross-check (1,000 games, machine checked quiet by process list -- the same persistent ~2.7-core Virtualization.framework process noted in tier1-arm-c-prime's own TimeMs run was present, no other duels-arena/training process was) read +9.4 Elo [-12.2, +30.9], also Inconclusive at that sample size. A lambda=1.0 control sibling (tier1-gen3-l10) trained from the IDENTICAL corpus does not clear the gating bar against v3 (-10.8 Elo, Inconclusive), and this generation beats that sibling directly by +35.4 Elo [+20.1, +50.7] (AcceptH1) -- confirming the lambda=0.5 blend, not fresh corpus content on its own, is what carries this generation's edge, consistent with v3's own promotion story. Frozen reference panel (candidate at nodes:2000): vs frozen v2@nodes:32000 reads -1.7 Elo [-25.8, +22.3] (Continue) -- notably LESS negative than v3's own -34.4 in this identical cell, a secondary positive signal; vs frozen v2@nodes:2000 reads +81.3 Elo [+59.2, +103.4] (AcceptH1); vs mcts-eval@nodes:8000 reads +142.4 Elo [+116.3, +168.5] (AcceptH1) -- decisively positive in absolute terms, but WEAKER than v3's own +196.4 reading against the identical panel member; vs mcts-uct@nodes:8000 reads +229.8 Elo [+200.3, +259.3] (AcceptH1), again WEAKER than v3's own +260.0. Elo readings against a common third party are not strictly transitive/comparable across generations (documented elsewhere in this project's history), so this is flagged as a caveat a human should weigh, not read as a contradiction of the direct win over v3. c-sweep (3 candidates, 1,000 games each at nodes:2000, vs the shipped default c=0.15): c=0.10 reads -1.4 Elo [-22.9, +20.1] (Continue), c=0.20 reads -12.8 Elo [-34.4, +8.7] (AcceptH0, worse), c=0.25 reads -26.8 Elo [-48.4, -5.2] (AcceptH0, worse) -- 0.15 stays the default, matching v3's own c-sweep verdict. TAKEN TOGETHER (initial read): a real, small, diminishing-returns generation, not a repeat of Generation 2's clean, large jump -- this project's own stop-rule prediction largely bearing out. REVISED, HELD NOT PROMOTED: a second, independent architect review -- commissioned to design a safe autonomous multi-generation promotion gate -- proposed a frozen-panel non-regression check as a required gate stage (a head-to-head win against the immediate parent alone is not sufficient once a panel predating that parent exists), applied it to this exact generation as a worked test case, and found the pooled regression against the two non-ancestor panel members (mcts-eval, mcts-uct) statistically real (pooled z roughly -3.0) -- disqualifying under that stage even though the direct v3 head-to-head is a clean AcceptH1. duels-value's DEFAULT_WEIGHTS stays v3.bin. This generation's weights, corpus, and full measurement stay archived and reachable (mcts-value:weights=gen3-l05) as a held, not discarded, result -- the champion is unchanged, so nothing about the data this generation produced is invalidated, and a future generation's larger data window (see docs/roadmap.md's autonomous-loop design) can build on it.

generations.notes: Recipe-calibration-day retrain (docs/roadmap.md's 'Autonomous self-play loop design', 'Recommended next step'): the IDENTICAL tier1-gen3-explore corpus and --value-target-lambda 0.5 as tier1-gen3-l05, retrained with tools/train_value.py's new fixed recipe -- 30 epochs, 2-epoch linear warm-up then cosine decay to a 2e-5 LR floor (--lr-floor 2e-5 --warmup-epochs 2), no patience-based early stopping (--no-patience), and SWA weight-averaging over the final third of epochs (--swa-tail-frac 0.333). Zero other variables changed from tier1-gen3-l05, so this isolates the recipe fix's own effect. Per-epoch training-loss logging (new in this recipe) shows train loss falling smoothly through all 30 epochs (0.510 -> 0.483) while validation loss plateaus after roughly epoch 10 (0.519 -> 0.507, essentially flat 0.5066-0.5070 from epoch 10 on) -- confirms the roadmap's diagnosis that patience was stopping on early-epoch noise, not real convergence, but the schedule actually reaching its floor bought only a marginal offline gain: best single epoch (27) read 0.50656, SWA over the last 10 epochs read 0.50650 (marginally lower, so SWA shipped per this recipe's automatic rule) -- a 0.00044 improvement over tier1-gen3-l05's own 0.50694, smaller than the 0.0011 training-seed-replicate noise floor documented in docs/roadmap.md, so not even clearly a real offline gain, let alone a guaranteed arena one. HONEST HEADLINE: gated head-to-head against the actual current champion (v3) at nodes:2000, pooled across two disjoint seed ranges (4,000 games, elo1=10): +14.9 Elo [+4.1, +25.6], AcceptH1, mechanism Pass -- a real win over v3, but NOT distinguishably better than tier1-gen3-l05's own +17.2 Elo reading in the identical comparison (heavily overlapping CIs). The clean, direct test -- this candidate vs tier1-gen3-l05 head-to-head, isolating the recipe change with literally nothing else different -- reads -6.4 Elo [-17.2, +4.3], AcceptH0 (rejects a positive effect at elo1=10), mechanism Pass: the recipe fix does NOT measurably improve arena strength over the old patience-based recipe on this corpus, and the point estimate leans (not significantly) slightly negative. Frozen reference panel reads in the same direction: vs frozen v2@nodes:32000 -16.1 Elo [-40.1,+8.0] (AcceptH0, vs tier1-gen3-l05's own -1.7), vs frozen v2@nodes:2000 +75.4 [+53.4,+97.5] (vs gen3-l05's +81.3), vs mcts-eval@nodes:8000 +125.8 [+100.2,+151.5] (vs gen3-l05's +142.4), vs mcts-uct@nodes:8000 +230.4 [+200.9,+260.0] (vs gen3-l05's +229.8, about even) -- weaker or even on 3 of 4 panel cells, matching the direct head-to-head's slightly-negative-but-inconclusive read rather than contradicting it. CONCLUSION: the training-recipe fix (annealing schedule reaching a real floor, no patience, SWA tail-averaging, train-loss logging) is a real hygiene/reproducibility improvement -- it removes reliance on patience's noise-selection and gives an honest overfitting/underfitting signal for the first time -- but on this one isolated trial it produced NO detectable arena-Elo gain over the old recipe, and the offline log-loss 'improvement' it shipped on is itself smaller than the measured training-seed noise floor. This is a genuine, useful negative result for the recipe-calibration exercise, not a failure to hide: see docs/roadmap.md's recipe-calibration-day write-up for the full reasoning and recommendation (ship the fixed recipe going forward for reproducibility, but do not expect it alone to move Elo; the data-scaling diagnostic run alongside this -- 50k/100k/200k games, val win-logloss 0.51823/0.50650/0.50335 -- points at a growing replay window, not the recipe, as the lever actually worth pursuing next).

diagnostics.note: Four offline diagnostics run alongside this retrain, all from tier1-gen3-explore (and tier1-arm-bc-explore for the 200k data point), same recipe as this entry unless noted, val win-log-loss reported (lower is better):

a_patience_vs_fixed_schedule.verdict: Marginal offline improvement (0.00044), smaller than the 0.0011 training-seed-replicate noise floor -- not clearly a real offline gain, and the gating battery above found no detectable arena-Elo gain either.

b_data_scaling.verdict: Monotonic, clear improvement with more data at every step measured, with no sign of plateauing by 200k -- the single clearest, best-supported diagnostic result. Points at data-starvation (a replay window > 1 generation) as the most promising lever, not the training recipe.

c_capacity.verdict: Bigger is not better -- hidden=256 reads worse on validation despite a lower training loss (0.469 vs 0.483 for 128), a mild overfitting signature. hidden=64 matches hidden=128. Not capacity-limited.

d_regularization.verdict: 1e-4 is a lateral move (within noise); 1e-3 is clearly worse on both train and val loss (underfitting). Not under-regularized at the current 1e-5.

diagnostics.overall_verdict: Of {label-noise/overfitting, under-regularization, data-starvation, capacity-limited}, the evidence points most clearly at data-starvation: val loss keeps falling with more data and shows no plateau yet at 200k games, while capacity and regularization changes in either direction do not help (and often hurt). A mild overfitting signature is present (train loss keeps falling past where val loss flattens, worse at 50k games and at hidden=256) but it reads as downstream of data-starvation (the train/val gap shrinks, not grows, going from 100k to 200k games) rather than an independent capacity or regularization problem.
